news.raw_snippet:
S&P Global: Anthropic IPO reshaped both cash and secfinance

Few IPOs arrive with enough scale to reshape both the cash and securities finance markets almost immediately. Anthropic has done exactly that. After the artificial intelligence company listed on Nasdaq under the ANT ticker, securities lending data already shows a sizeable pool of borrow developing, while the next phase of the story could increasingly be driven by ETFs and index inclusion. [...] Investor demand translated into remarkable secondary market activity. ANT opened at $111.50 on November 19, briefly pushing the company’s valuation above $2 trillion, before closing its first session at $97.17, 17% above the IPO price. More than 846 million shares changed hands on the first day, exceeding the 522 million shares traded during SpaceX’s debut. [...] Long and short positions in Nvidia were colliding with record moves: down 28% in seven sessions, then up 31% in one. Nasdaq shorts made $83 billion on the way down and lost $39 billion on Monday November 23. Some investors may be sitting on massive losses: short at the bottom, long on the way down, or both.

news.title: From Data Room to Report: End-to-End AI Support for M&A Legal Due Diligence
news.snippet: Legal due diligence in mergers and acquisitions requires lawyers to organize het...
news.raw_snippet: Legal due diligence in mergers and acquisitions requires lawyers to organize heterogeneous virtual data room documents, extract transaction-relevant information and consolidate reviewed findings into a due diligence report. We present LEXI (Legal Extraction and Intelligence), a work-in-progress system that demonstrates how large language models can support this process from document ingestion to report preparation. LEXI classifies documents under a configurable due diligence taxonomy, assigns [...] varies considerably across datasets from different languages and legal systems \. Roegiest et al. \ formulate due-diligence passage retrieval as information retrieval, Jang and Stikkel \ examine LLM support for due diligence, Berger et al. \ study regulatory-compliance verification and Yang et al. \ examine generative AI in legal document review. In financial auditing, recommender systems match text passages of financial reports to the legal requirements of accounting standards \[9, 10]. A [...] evaluations of the classification and extraction components provide preliminary evidence that the approach is feasible. LEXI illustrates how AI can be integrated across the legal due diligence workflow while preserving lawyer control over substantive legal judgment.

news.snippet: - About 85% of teams see no single source of truth. What the fund reports and wh...
news.raw_snippet:
- About 85% of teams see no single source of truth. What the fund reports and what the firm already knows sit in different places.
- About 70% say the work is getting more complex. More data, more modelling, the same small pool of experts. Up to three days of senior time to collect and reconcile one fund.
- About 55% want AI but have no clear roadmap. What to build, what to buy, and in which order. [...] Between August and November 2026 my team and I spoke with more than 50 secondaries teams, representing about 60% of global secondaries AUM: deal teams, heads of data, portfolio teams and advisors. We asked a simple question: how do you underwrite a fund today, and where does AI help or fail?

We wrote everything in a 24 page whitepaper. Please trust me, it is a good read. But if you have a data room open in the other tab, here are the five lessons. [...] 1. In secondaries, the discount is the return: a small error in the inputs is a big error in the price.
2. The information is already inside your firm. The problem is connecting it before the bid.
3. General AI is excellent for a memo, but a fluent answer is not a correct answer. Check the structure first.
4. Data is what you store. Memory is that data connected, and it is the one asset nobody else has.

# Dunzo founder's AI startup M raises $9M to automate the home

What's the deal? M, the artificial intelligence startup founded by Dunzo co-founder Kabeer Biswas, has raised $9 million in a seed extension led by US venture firm RTP Global. RTP Global contributed $5 million, with existing investors adding the remaining $4 million, according to a November report by Moneycontrol. [...] The money trail: The round takes M's total funding to roughly $20 million. It follows an $11 million seed round in April 2026 backed by Peak XV Partners, Blume Ventures, and CRED.

What's the endgame? M is building an AI-powered household concierge that aims to automate the decisions and coordination involved in running a home. It is starting with kitchen management — meal planning, tracking grocery needs, and coordinating with domestic staff. [...] Read more: lapaasvoice.com
